tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search Cbest's catalog of real lighting products from every brand it carries. Accepts Persian or English. Returns normalized facets (mounting, indoor/outdoor, IP, colour temperature, and wattage/lumen where stated) plus what the query matched on. Colour temperature is returned but is NOT filterable:

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Every field on file for one product, by the id search_products returns ('brand/product-slug'), including provenance: whether the fact came from the brand's own website or from a page of its PDF catalog, and when it was read.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The 20 canonical categories with Persian and English names, product counts, and which brands have products in each. Small enough to fetch once and reason over the whole catalog; flags categories that only one brand covers.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: Every brand whose products are in Cbest's catalog, with what it covers, how complete its data is, and when it was last read. A brand is a maker, not a party the customer is referred to: Cbest sells these products itself. No contact details — see the server instructions.

tools.name: get_brand
tools.description: One brand in full: what they make, the product families they run, and — the field worth the call — doesNotDo, a statement of what they genuinely do NOT make, computed from absence in their product list rather than inferred from their marketing.

tools.name: compare_brands
tools.description: Which brands have products in a category, with counts, share, and per-facet data coverage. Coverage describes what each brand's SOURCE stated, never product quality, and a one-brand category says so rather than pretending to be a comparison.

tools.name: classify_lighting_term
tools.description: Map any Persian or English lighting phrase onto the canonical taxonomy — «داون‌لایت توکار», 'trimless plaster frame', 'high bay'. Backed by 522 learned type→category pairs plus rules measured at 95% agreement. Returns null for a phrase that names no category rather than guessing.

tools.name: start_consultation
tools.description: Turn a described need into a link the person opens themselves: a consultation with Cbest's adviser, prefilled with the need. The adviser knows the whole catalog, answers with real products and builds a list of materials; Cbest then checks price and stock and issues the quote itself. Nobody is handed

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Turn a list of products you already found (ids from search_products) into a link the person opens themselves, prefilled with those products, so Cbest's adviser continues from the list and Cbest issues a quote after checking price and stock. Returns NO price and NO stock, places no order, and stores

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "search_products" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "search_products" appears informational but accepts parameters (environment) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: q, category, brand, environment, mounting, ip_min, price_tier, has_image, limit, offset

findings.title: Hidden characters in tool description
findings.detail: Description of "classify_lighting_term" contains 1 invisible/zero-width or bidi character(s). Legitimate descriptions have no reason to hide text the model still reads.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "request_quote" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_consultation, request_quote · Private data: get_product, list_brands, start_consultation · Public sink: compare_brands, start_consultation · Destructive: get_brand.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_consultation, request_quote · Private data: get_product, list_brands, start_consultation · Public sink: compare_brands, start_consultation · Destructive: get_brand

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.detail: Tool "search_products" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
